newTerms.the one God (lowercase one): el único Dios / un solo Dios (kept apart from «Dios Único» for capitalized One God)

forcedChoices.reason: The English uses lowercase for Amenemope's title; the glossary short form allows it.

forcedChoices.choice: «las tradiciones de Caligastia y de la rebelión de Lucifer»
forcedChoices.reason: English 'the Caligastia and the Lucifer rebellion' can read as two rebellions; the Spanish keeps Caligastia as a separate tradition and does not add a second 'rebelión'.

forcedChoices.choice: «el mal quedaba claramente sumergido, en la eternidad»
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish 'este' would be ambiguous between evil and goodness; the English 'it' refers to evil, so the noun is repeated.
'hyphenate their gods' depends on the written form of compound god names; Spanish needs the word 'nombres' to carry it.
The English refers to the word itself; Spanish 'juicio' carries the same sense, so no English word in parentheses is needed.

forcedChoices.choice: «Él es el misericordioso…» with capital É
forcedChoices.reason: Capital only because it starts a sentence inside the quote; other pronouns for God stay lowercase.
